title: Operadic universal property of Day convolution
statement:
Use smallness, monoidal infinity categories and inert-preserving algebra functors as in [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the generalized nonsymmetric operads of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. In the generalized-operad convention, the degree-zero fibre is a Kan space, inert edges are cocartesian over consecutive-subinterval maps, and the incidence-diagram axiom includes both vertex and edge projections. For a small monoidal infinity category $C$, put $P(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$, where $\mathcal S$ is the infinity category of small spaces. Then $P(C)$ admits Day convolution, with tensor given by left Kan extension of the external cartesian product along tensor on $C$; it preserves small colimits separately and the Yoneda embedding is strong monoidal. Let $\mathcal O\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be any small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad. Let $C^{\mathrm{op},\otimes}$ be the cocartesian fibration obtained by taking the opposite of each fibre of $C^\otimes$, keeping its base $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. There is an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}(P(C))\simeq\operatorname{Mon}_{\mathcal O\times_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}C^{\mathrm{op},\otimes}}(\mathcal S).$$
Here the right side is the full subcategory of space-valued functors $M$ such that the inert projections from $(o;c_1,\ldots,c_n)$ give an equivalence $M(o;\boldsymbol c)\simeq\prod_{i=1}^nM(o_i;c_i)$, with the empty product a point. On a colour $(o;c)$ the functor is evaluation of the coefficient presheaf of the algebra at $c$. The equivalence is natural in operad maps, strong monoidal functors of $C$, and all coherent transformations. If $F:C\to\mathcal V$ is strong monoidal and $\mathcal V$ is locally small, cocomplete, and has tensor preserving small colimits separately, its colimit-preserving Yoneda extension $F_!:P(C)\to\mathcal V$ is strong monoidal. It has the lax monoidal right adjoint $v\mapsto(c\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(F(c),v))$, naturally in $F$.

proof.text: Take as $P(C)^\otimes$ the coherent Day structure $Q_C\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ of [lem-coef-day-relative-exponential-model], the pullback of the right-fibration envelope along the algebra classifying $C^\otimes$; this is how the source defines Day convolution. Its fibre over $[r]$ is $P(C)^r$, and its binary operation is the left Kan extension of the external cartesian product along tensor on $C$, so it is a Day convolution in the sense of the statement. By [lem-coef-day-model-yoneda-strong-monoidal], every operation of $Q_C$ preserves small colimits separately in each variable, and the Yoneda functor has a fully faithful strong monoidal enhancement $j^\otimes:C^\otimes\to Q_C$, whose comparisons $\star_rj^r\simeq jc_r$ form a morphism of unital planar operation systems. Smallness is as fixed in [def-coef-complete-algebroid]; the larger universe used to form $Q_C$ changes no colimit shape, and the presheaf values remain small spaces.

source.place: Section 5, first paragraph: Day convolution on P(C) defined as the pullback of RFib along the algebra classifying C^tensor, and its universal-property formula preceding Proposition 5.1

proof.text:
Use the right-fibration model of [lem-coef-day-relative-exponential-model]. With $S=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ and the coherent classifying algebra $\underline C:S\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}^\times$, put $Q_C=S\times_{\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}^\times}\operatorname{RFib}^\times$. This is the genuine infinity-categorical pullback of coherent functors, with its identification data. The cited model makes $Q_C\to S$ monoidal cocartesian, with fibre $P(C)^n$, Day block operations and the stated inert-arrow criterion. This is the $P(C)^\otimes$ chosen in step 1. Its hypotheses on spaces need no extra assumption: [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion] at the terminal category gives small colimits in $\mathcal S$, and [lem-coef-space-presheaf-cocompletion] gives $X\times-\dashv\operatorname{Map}(X,-)$. For $Y=\operatorname{colim}_eY_e$, adjunction gives $\operatorname{Map}(X\times Y,Z)\simeq\lim_e\operatorname{Map}(Y_e,\operatorname{Map}(X,Z))\simeq\lim_e\operatorname{Map}(X\times Y_e,Z)$; the cocone criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] proves separate product cocontinuity.

Let $q:\mathcal O\to S$, and write $\underline C_q=\underline Cq$. Apply the total-product functor of [lem-coef-generalized-cartesian-product-cones] with target $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$ to obtain the coherent functor $D:\mathcal O\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$, $D(o)=C^n$ over $[n]$. Its block maps are those of $C^\otimes$. By [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], the cocartesian unstraightening of $D^{\mathrm{op}}:o\mapsto D(o)^{\mathrm{op}}$ is $T=\mathcal O\times_S C^{\mathrm{op},\otimes}$; this takes fibrewise opposites and keeps the base fixed. This is also a generalized operad in the convention of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]: inert lifts are pairs of inert lifts, the incidence diagrams are the products of the two incidence diagrams, and the zero fibre is the Kan space $\mathcal O_{[0]}$.

An algebra $A:\mathcal O\to Q_C$ gives an inert-preserving $B_A:\mathcal O\to\operatorname{RFib}^\times$ together with its coherent identification $p^\times B_A\simeq\underline C_q$. Apply the product-cone equivalence with target $\operatorname{RFib}$ to get a monoid $\Phi_A=\Pi B_A:\mathcal O\to\operatorname{RFib}$ over $D$; naturality in the finite-product-preserving $p$ gives the identification $p\Phi_A\simeq D$. The section-classification equivalence of the Day-model node now constructs an actual coherent $M_A:T\to\mathcal S$. At $(o;c_1,\ldots,c_n)$ it is the fibre of the product right fibration $\prod_i E_{A(o_i)}\to C^n$, hence $\prod_i A(o_i)(c_i)$. This constructs evaluation from the universal right-fibration family and includes every simplex. Its inert projections are product projections and its zero-degree value is a point, so $M_A$ is multiplicative. Equivalently, apply the classifier once to the universal product right fibration over $Q_C$, obtaining $\epsilon_C:Q_C\times_S C^{\mathrm{op},\otimes}\to\mathcal S$, and restrict it along $A\times\mathrm{id}$. Its product cones lift coherently to $\mathcal S^\times$ by [lem-coef-generalized-cartesian-product-cones].

source.place: Notation 6.1, Definition 6.14, Corollary 6.10; Proposition 6.18, first three equivalences. Evaluation via the section classifier cited in that proof, and the agent generalized-incidence formulation.

proof.text:
Conversely let $M:T\to\mathcal S$ be multiplicative. Apply the inverse of the section-classification equivalence in [lem-coef-day-relative-exponential-model] for the fixed coherent $D$ of step 2. It produces an actual coherent section $\Phi_M:\mathcal O\to\operatorname{RFib}$ over $D$, whose value at $o$ is a right fibration $E_o\to C^n$ classifying $M(o;-)$, with all transition maps already present. We check the product condition on this section. The inert projections give a coherent square
$$\begin{matrix}E_o&\longrightarrow&\prod_iE_{o_i}\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
D(o)&\xrightarrow{\sim}&\prod_iD(o_i).\end{matrix}$$
The lower equivalence is the product cone for $D$, and both vertical arrows are right fibrations. Pull the right-hand fibration back along the lower equivalence. By the space-transport classification [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], its comparison with $E_o$ is the transformation whose component at $(c_i)$ is precisely $M(o;(c_i))\to\prod_iM(o_i;c_i)$. These components are equivalences by multiplicativity. The componentwise equivalence criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore makes this a presheaf equivalence, hence an equivalence of right fibrations. Cartesian transport in the Day-model node takes the lower base equivalence to an equivalence in $\operatorname{RFib}$, so the original product comparison is an equivalence as well. At degree zero, $D(o)=*$ and $E_o$ is the terminal space because $M(o;*)$ is terminal. Thus $\Phi_M$ is a monoid in $\operatorname{RFib}$, over the fixed monoid $D$; this uses no terminality of $\mathcal O_{[0]}$.

Apply the inverse product-cone equivalence of [lem-coef-generalized-cartesian-product-cones] with target $\operatorname{RFib}$. It produces the whole coherent inert-preserving $B_M:\mathcal O\to\operatorname{RFib}^\times$. Its naturality under the product-preserving $p$ supplies $p^\times B_M\simeq\underline C_q$, since the specified product-cone inverse for $D$ is $\underline C_q$. The defining infinity-categorical pullback of $Q_C$ consequently gives $A_M:\mathcal O\to Q_C$. The inert criterion of the Day-model node says that it is an algebra. On a colour it is the presheaf $c\mapsto M(o;c)$. For an output block $I_j$ of a base arrow, the right-fibration square supplies the natural transformation $\prod_{i\in I_j}A_M(o_i)(c_i)\to A_M(o'_j)(\bigotimes_{i\in I_j}c_i)$, whose left-Kan adjunct is its Day operation. Composing with the presheaf map for $d_j\to\bigotimes_{i\in I_j}c_i$ gives evaluation on a general arrow of $T$. Empty blocks give a map from the Day unit. These formulas describe the existing section and product-cone constructions; no simplex is manufactured by choosing unrelated decompositions at its edges.

source.place: Proposition 6.18, right-fibration square and fibrewise comparison at the end of the proof; Proposition 5.1 and Remark 5.16. Agent generalized-incidence extension includes each zero-degree object separately.

proof.text:
The constructions in steps 2 and 3 are inverse on infinity categories. More explicitly, the pullback defining $Q_C$ identifies its algebra category with the infinity-categorical fibre over $\underline C_q$ of
$$\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}(\operatorname{RFib}^\times)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}(\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}^\times);$$
the inert-arrow criterion in [lem-coef-day-relative-exponential-model] checks exactly the algebra condition in this identification. Naturality of [lem-coef-generalized-cartesian-product-cones] for $p$ identifies this fibre with the fibre over $D$ of $\operatorname{Mon}_{\mathcal O}(\operatorname{RFib})\to\operatorname{Mon}_{\mathcal O}(\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U})$. The Day-model node's section classifier is an equivalence on the full category of sections over $D$, including all mapping spaces. The square checked in step 3 shows in both directions that its full subcategory of monoid sections corresponds exactly to the multiplicative functors $T\to\mathcal S$. Restrict that equivalence to these full subcategories. This proves the asserted equivalence, its evaluation on colours, and its inverse, including transformations and higher simplices. In particular the inverse comparisons come from specified units and counits of these functor-category equivalences, rather than independently chosen maps of coefficient objects. Their evaluations at every colour are the presheaf classification identities; at $[0]$ they are identities of terminal objects. The componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] detects them as equivalences. No essential-image factorization or identification with a raw relative exponential is used.

An operad map changes $D$ and $T$ by base change, so naturality follows from the two cited equivalences' base-change naturality. For a strong monoidal $H:C'\to C$, cartesian transport of right fibrations restricts every coefficient presheaf along $H^{\mathrm{op}}$, and products of those pullbacks are again the corresponding pullbacks. The coherent restriction and evaluation clause in the Day-model node therefore gives the lax monoidal map $Q_C\to Q_{C'}$ and identifies its effect under the comparison with precomposition by $\mathcal O\times_S C'^{\mathrm{op},\otimes}\to T$. Its block map is the adjunct of $\prod_iF_i(Hc'_i)\to G(\bigotimes_iHc'_i)\simeq G(H(\bigotimes_ic'_i))$. All parameter simplices are part of the section and product-cone equivalences. This proves the required coefficient naturality without asserting that presheaf restriction is strong monoidal.

source.place: Proposition 6.18, Lemma 6.20 and Corollary 6.21; coherent-fibre proof follows the right-fibration construction, with generalized-operad naturality as in Haugseng 2311.13362 Section 5.

proof.text: For the strong monoidal extension, use unital planar operation systems and their specified projection-pullback normal form from [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence] for $C,P(C),\mathcal V$; denote their reduced operations by $c_r,p_r,v_r$. First [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion] gives $L=F_!$ with $Lj\simeq F$. For every $r\geq0$, the finite-variable restriction equivalence in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion], with no relations on each copy of $C$, compares separately cocontinuous functors $P(C)^r\to\mathcal V$ with functors $C^r\to\mathcal V$, including all transformation spaces and compatibility homotopies. Its use requires only cocompleteness of $\mathcal V$. On the $r$ reduced variables, $Lp_r$ and $v_r L^r$ preserve colimits separately: $L$ preserves colimits, the Day operations do so by step 1, and the operations of $\mathcal V$ do so by the tensor hypothesis and induction. Their restrictions have the coherent equivalence $Lp_rj^r\simeq L j c_r\simeq F c_r\simeq v_r F^r\simeq v_rL^rj^r$, using the planar-compatible strong Yoneda enhancement into $Q_C$ from [lem-coef-day-model-yoneda-strong-monoidal] and the strong structure of $F$. Lift these comparisons and their entire planar-tree compatibility diagrams through the finite-variable equivalences. For an $r$-input planar tree every external variable occurs exactly once; thus each composite on either side remains separately cocontinuous in precisely those $r$ variables, including when a subtree is nullary. Full faithfulness identifies the spaces of compatibility simplices with their already specified boundaries, and therefore lifts the coherent tree diagrams, grafting data, contractions and unary identities. The generic mapping-space fact used here is the first paragraph of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. For $r=0$ the restriction is the identity equivalence of $\mathcal V$ and the comparison is $L j(\mathbf1_C)\simeq F(\mathbf1_C)\simeq\mathbf1_{\mathcal V}$; no cocontinuity of a constant functor on unused variables is claimed. Only after these reduced comparisons have been lifted, pull them back along the block projections specified by the normal-form lemma, including all its higher pullback data. Its final assertion turns them into a coherent transformation of the classifying diagrams with components $L^n$, hence a functor of unstraightenings preserving every cocartesian edge. This is the strong monoidal enhancement in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. The same lifting of complete coherent diagrams includes transformations of $F$.

source.place: Proposition 6.26 and Remark 6.27; agent reduced-planar-tree extension following the established monoidal-Yoneda split.

proof.text: Define $R(v)(c)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(F(c),v)$; local smallness makes this a small-space-valued presheaf, and the mapping bifunctor of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] makes it coherent in both variables. For a density cocone $G\simeq\operatorname{colim}_e j(c_e)$ from [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density], the cocone criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] and Yoneda evaluation give $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(F_!G,v)\simeq\lim_e\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(F(c_e),v)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{P(C)}(G,R(v))$, with the limits over the opposite density diagram. Both comparisons are induced by the cocones, hence are natural in $G$ and $v$. On the fibre at $[n]$ the right adjoint of $F_!^n$ is $R^n$: mapping spaces in a product are products, so the preceding adjunction applies in each factor; at $[0]$ both fibres are terminal. Apply [lem-coef-monoidal-relative-adjoint-inert] to the strong monoidal $F_!^\otimes:Q_C\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ of step 5, whose underlying functor has the right adjoint $R$. It gives a right adjoint relative to $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ with fibre $R^n$ over $[n]$, whose coherent unit, counit and triangle homotopies lie over the identity of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and agree on fibres with the given adjunctions, as in [lem-coef-cocartesian-relative-right-adjoint]. The inert theorem also proves that this relative right adjoint preserves inert edges, hence is lax monoidal as defined in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and identifies its operation comparisons as mates of tensors of counits. Explicitly $R(v)\otimes_{\mathrm{Day}}R(w)\to R(v\otimes w)$ is adjoint to $F_!(R(v)\otimes_{\mathrm{Day}}R(w))\simeq F_!R(v)\otimes F_!R(w)\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_v\otimes\varepsilon_w}v\otimes w$, and its unit is adjoint to $F_!(\mathbf1_{P(C)})\simeq\mathbf1_{\mathcal V}$. The relative triangle and strong monoidal coherences supply their lax coherences. A transformation $F\to F'$ gives $F_!\to F'_!$ by free cocompletion and $R_{F'}\to R_F$ by precomposition in the displayed mapping spaces; these are mates, including all higher transformations. This is the claimed naturality, with the right-adjoint variable contravariant.
